name: Rosé des Riceys

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Pinot Noir sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
Most Champagne is non-vintage, a blend of several years for a steady house style. In great years a house may declare a vintage and bottle wine from that harvest alone.
White from white grapes. In Champagne, 100% Chardonnay.
White wine made only from black grapes. In Champagne, Pinot Noir, Meunier or both.
How sweet a sparkling wine is after dosage: Extra Brut under 6 g of sugar a liter, Brut under 12, Demi-sec 32 to 50. Brut is the most common.

notes: Chardonnay gives Champagne acidity and a biscuit flavor, and Meunier adds body, richness and fruit.
Houses blend grapes and villages to keep the same non-vintage style from year to year.
Champagne is pale even when made from red grapes, because the juice is pressed gently with little skin contact.
A dosage of sugar and wine sets the sweetness, and today it is used mostly to fine-tune the sense of acidity.
Rosé Champagne has a blush color, a fruity aroma and an earthy flavor.

blurb.text: A rosé from the three villages of Les Riceys in the Aube, in Champagne, made only from Pinot Noir. It can be aged in tank for early drinking or in wood for longer keeping, and has a distinctive taste the French call goût des Riceys.
